transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Michael Tran (Redwood AE), Priya Ramesh (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood SE), Rajesh Kumar (FinSight Head of ML), Emily Stone (FinSight Eng Mgr), Oliver Park (FinSight Infra), Maya Li (FinSight Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Redwood performed benchmark comparison vs customer's baseline provider. Median latency and throughput favorable to Redwood Dedicated/opt path. Observed higher tail latency on long sequences; possible causes: KV cache cold starts, batching configuration, and model variant differences. Agreed next steps include 99th percentile tests, replay dataset, and infra deep-dive.

[00:00] Michael Tran: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick run through of the benchmark results we dropped last evening, and then go into tuning recommendations and next steps. Rajesh, thanks for being here.
[00:15] Rajesh Kumar: Yeah thanks Mike, quick note - we got the spreadsheet, skimmed it. A lot to unpack, uh can you start with the headline numbers?
[00:28] Priya Ramesh: Sure. So headline, using your replay, on Redwood Dedicated with the quantized 8-bit model we saw median latency around ~120ms for the 512 token tail (per-request median) vs your baseline provider median of ~220ms. Throughput measured at ~4.8k tokens/sec sustained on the Dedicated pool vs baseline ~3.5k tokens/sec under same replay.
[00:52] Emily Stone: Those medians look great, what about 95th and 99th? That's really what worries us for prod.
[01:05] Priya Ramesh: Right - 95th was ~320ms on our run, baseline was ~500ms. 99th is the sticky spot - we're seeing spikes up to 1.1s in some runs, baseline had around 1.3s. So better but still not within your 500ms SLO target.
[01:28] Oliver Park: When you say spikes, is that cold-starts or steady-state? Our concern is steady-state tail latency on sustained traffic.
[01:40] Priya Ramesh: Good question. We correlated traces - there are a few patterns: prefix cache misses (your workload has high variability in prompts), some bursty requests that force smaller batch sizes, and occasional small GC/CPU contention on control plane when KV cache warmup hits. Not classic cold-starts; more like per-shard KV cache warmup and batching inefficiencies.
[02:03] Carlos Vega: Also worth noting our benchmark used model variant rdx-v1-8q which is quantized and optimized. There are small diff in model outputs vs baseline; we put the eval diff sheet in the spreadsheet but it's within your quality tolerance based on the eval prompts you shared.
[02:24] Maya Li: Can you confirm there was no function calling or heavy tool-calling in this replay? We use a fair amount of tool calls in prod.
[02:33] Priya Ramesh: Correct, this replay was pure text gen. If tool-calling is in the loop, latency patterns change a bit since you get external I/O and serialize different steps. We can run a replay that includes tool-call patterns if you provide the traces.
[02:47] Rajesh Kumar: Ok. On the throughput numbers, how was batching configured? We saw on the sheet batch size max of 64 - is that server-side only or did you tune client side?
[02:58] Priya Ramesh: Server side continuous batching with max_batch=64, dynamic time-slicing to balance latency. For your workload we found aggressive batching up to 48 gave best cost/latency tradeoff; beyond that latency increases for smaller requests. We included recommended batching profiles per route in the sheet.
[03:17] Emily Stone: You mentioned KV cach in the doc - did you see a lot of KV cache misses?
[03:25] Priya Ramesh: Yeah, and small typo in the doc - KV cach (sic). We saw about 12% miss rate in the replay due to many unique prefixes; that translates to repeated autoregress steps happening on the GPU rather than cache hits which increases tail. If you can standardize prompts or enable prefix caching at the app-level we can reduce that.
[03:45] Rajesh Kumar: For the 99th percentile you saw 1.1s - what's the breakdown? Is that network, queuing, or model compute?
[03:55] Priya Ramesh: Breakdown in the spreadsheet: ~60% model compute (longer sequences hitting non-optimized kernels), ~25% queuing/batching delays during bursts, ~15% misc (control plane latency, minor infra jitter). We can dig into kernel-level traces with your infra team.
[04:15] Oliver Park: On the infrastructure side, our cluster is in GCP in region us-west2, same as your test. Any cross-region differences?
[04:24] Michael Tran: We kept region constant to remove variability. We did one cross-region run and saw an extra 10-20ms network overhead but not material to the 99th percentiles you're worried about.
[04:36] Carlos Vega: Quick clarification - baseline provider in your sheet was VendorX right? We tried to match instance types but there are small infra differences which we've annotated.
[04:47] Rajesh Kumar: Yes baseline is VendorX, they gave us reserved instances on A100s. We saw VendorX had worse throughput but similar tail in some windows.
[05:00] Priya Ramesh: One area to improve tail: we recommend a small config change - enable hot-kernel prefetch and adjust micro-batching windows for routes with high prefix variance. That typically reduces 99th by ~20-30% in our customers runs. We'll need to test on your replay to confirm.
[05:20] Emily Stone: If we enable those changes, does it increase cost? Any tradeoffs?
[05:27] Priya Ramesh: Slightly higher GPU cycles during warm windows but overall cost per token often drops because we reduce wasted recompute. The spreadsheet includes cost model comparisons for both default and tuned configs.
[05:41] Rajesh Kumar: What about security/compliance? We asked about audit logs and KMS earlier. Did you run benchmarks on private deployment or hosted?
[05:52] Michael Tran: These runs were on Redwood Dedicated (customer-dedicated pool) in your VPC with customer-provided KMS for at-rest key management - audit logs were captured. We can also run the same on a private on-prem stack if needed; cost and perf differ.
[06:08] Maya Li: For our procurement, we'll want a pilot pricing number for a 3-month dedicated pool.
[06:15] Michael Tran: I'll send a pricing sheet for dedicated pilot options after this meeting - Michael will circle back with the options.
[06:23] Rajesh Kumar: Cool. Priya, can you walk through a specific example where the 99th spike happened?
[06:30] Priya Ramesh: Sure - take session id X-8492 in the replay: sequence 1024 tokens, with an unusual prompt prefix not seen in training. The first few autoregress steps missed the KV cache causing compute to re-eval earlier tokens, which pulled latency to >1 second. We logged kernel timings - non-optimized attention kernel invoked for those longer sequences.
[06:54] Carlos Vega: There's also a small delta between rdx-v1-8q outputs and vendor baseline; per the eval sheet it's a 0.6% difference on BLEU-like metric for your test set. Rajesh, you indicated that's acceptable?
[07:08] Rajesh Kumar: Yeah 0.6% is fine as long as failure modes are rare.
[07:13] Emily Stone: For canary and rollouts, can we do traffic shadowing to validate before full cutover?
[07:20] Michael Tran: Yes we support shadowing and can do canary with route-level rollouts and automatic fallback. We can set up a low-percent rollout first.
[07:30] Maya Li: About the replay to run 99th - what format do you need? Our infra team has logs and traces.
[07:36] Priya Ramesh: JSON trace with request/response payloads and timestamps; if you can strip any PII and provide 5-10k requests representing peak windows that's ideal. Oliver, can your team export that?
[07:47] Oliver Park: Yes we can. We'll pick representative windows from last week's peak.
[07:51] Priya Ramesh: Great - once we have that we'll run both steady-state and burst scenarios and attach per-request kernel timings.
[08:00] Rajesh Kumar: For the 99th improvement, you mentioned micro-batching. Are you suggesting increasing max batch size or shortening batching window?
[08:09] Priya Ramesh: Shortening the batching window for latency-critical routes while allowing larger batches for background or lower-priority routes. Also adaptive batching that switches behavior based on incoming QPS.
[08:21] Emily Stone: Ok that sounds sensible. How long will tuning runs take?
[08:25] Priya Ramesh: Each full replay run takes roughly 2-3 hours depending on length; we typically run a few repeats to remove noise. We'll prioritize the 99th-tail run first which should be done by Friday if we get the replay today.
[08:38] Michael Tran: Recap quick: Priya will run tail-latency tests and share updated spreadsheet; Michael will send pricing; customer will provide replay. Schedule infra deep-dive next week. Anything else?
[08:53] Rajesh Kumar: One ask - can you include an A/B with the baseline's quantization config? We want apples-to-apples on the quantized path too.
[09:01] Carlos Vega: Yes we'll match quantization settings and call that out.
[09:06] Maya Li: And include cost-per-100k tokens number please.
[09:10] Michael Tran: Will do.
[09:15] Emily Stone: Cool thanks all.
[09:18] Rajesh Kumar: Thanks.
[09:20] Michael Tran: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the sheet and with calendar invites for the infra deep-dive.

Meeting end.
